newsitem.title: USA: Guest Supply sees Q4 EPS at $0.22/shr.
newsitem.headline: Guest Supply sees Q4 EPS at $0.22/shr.

text.p: Guest Supply Inc said Wednesday its earnings in the fourth quarter should come in at about $0.22 per share, a drop it attributed to an inventory charge and a pricing adjustment.
The earnings projection is a 27 decline from earnings in the prior year's fourth quarter and would come in below analysts' estimates, it said.
During that same period, the company said it expects to report record revenues of $52.18 million, an eight percent increase over the same period in the prior year.
Guest Supply said a pre-tax, non-recurring charge of $650,000 to inventory and a pricing adjustment of $850,000 will cause the lower-than-expected fourth quarter results.
The company did not say what analysts' estimates were for the fourth quarter. It did not immediately return a telephone call.
According to First Call, the analysts' mean estimate for the fourth quarter was $0.35 per share.

The company said it expects its first quarter net income to exceed net income that was posted in the same period in the prior year by more than 20 percent. During the prior year's first quarter, the company reported net income of $944,000.
It also projected that its 1997 fiscal year earnings should be double the earnings it posted for the 1996 fiscal year.
Guest Supply President Clifford Stanley said in a statement that the fourth quarter ends what was a transitional year for the company.

"The fourth quarter began slowly, but throughout the month of September our order volume increased significantly," Stanley said. "First-quarter volume is strong and plant efficiency has improved. We expect to exceed last year's first-quarter net income by more than 20 percent. Last year's first quarter was our best first quarter ever and will be our most difficult comparison."
Guest Supply said it expects to release its fiscal 1996 fourth-quarter financial results on or about November 21.
